chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Take the pebbles of the Jamarat, then go to the furthest Jamarah which is near al-Aqabah, and throw them from its front, not from its top. And while the pebbles are in your hands, say: "O Allah, these are my pebbles, so count them for me and raise them in my deeds." Then throw, and with each pebble say: "Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, repel from me the Shaytan and his hosts. O Allah, for the confirmation of Your Book and upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, make it an accepted Hajj, a accepted deed, a thanked effort, and a forgiven sin. And let the distance between you and the Jamarah be the measure of ten cubits or fifteen cubits. When you reach your saddle (mount) and return from the throwing, say: "O Allah, in You I have trusted, and upon You I have relied. How excellent is the Lord, how excellent the Master, and how excellent the Helper."'
He said: 'And it is recommended that the Jamarat be thrown while in a state of purity (taharah).'

key_terms.الْجِمَارِ: The Jamarat (pillars/stones) at Mina where pebbles are thrown
key_terms.الْعَقَبَةِ: Al-Aqabah, a specific location near the furthest Jamarah
key_terms.حَصَى: Small pebbles used for Ramy al-Jamarat
key_terms.رَحْلَكَ: Your saddle/mount (referring to the camel or vehicle)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and methods for throwing pebbles at the Jamarat during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides the detailed jurisprudential framework for the *Rami al-Jamarat* ritual, emphasizing the spiritual significance of casting pebbles as a symbolic expulsion of Satan (*Idhhar al-Shaytan*) and affirmation of divine law. It highlights the recommended practice of performing this act while in a state of ritual purity (*Tahur*), linking physical cleanliness to spiritual devotion, and prescribes specific supplications that frame the act as both obedience to the Prophet's Sunnah and a means for securing an accepted Hajj (*Hajj Mabrur*).
